name: Mirchi Bajji (Chili Fritters)
instructions: 1. Slit the chilies lengthwise and remove the seeds if you prefer less heat. Soak them in salted tamarind water for 15 minutes to reduce spice levels.
2. Prepare the stuffing by mixing tamarind paste, cumin powder, and a pinch of salt.
3. Stuff the chilies with the prepared tamarind mixture.
4. In a bowl, whisk together gram flour, rice flour, red chili powder, carom seeds, salt, turmeric, and a pinch of baking soda.
5. Gradually add water to the flour mixture to create a thick, smooth batter.
6. Heat oil in a deep pan.
7. Dip the stuffed chilies into the batter, ensuring they are well coated.
8. Carefully drop them into the hot oil and fry until they turn crispy and golden brown.
9. Drain on paper towels and serve hot, often accompanied by chopped onions, cilantro, and lemon juice.
description: Mirchi Bajji is an iconic Andhra street food, famously served at tea stalls and beaches. It is a quintessential comfort snack, celebrated for its perfect balance of tangy, spicy, and savory flavors, often enjoyed during the monsoon season.
